content:
- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (especially when sentiment > 0.67); model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward quickly.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is consistently low or negative (sentiment < 0.33); model fails to recognize downward momentum.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overreacts to short-term volatility, then overcorrects, leading to lagged underestimation in subsequent periods.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag in price decline after sharp drops; model delays recognition of downward trend until 2–3 days after true price turns.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often overweights bullish signals, leading to premature peaks and subsequent overcorrection.
- Avoid extrapolating recent highs as sustainable; if sentiment is neutral or declining, reduce forecasted peak by 5–10% to account for mean reversion.
- If sentiment is high and price is rising, model tends to overforecast; if sentiment is high and price is falling, model undercorrects — adjust for sentiment-weighted volatility.
